verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. Defining r=p-x and applying the exact polynomial Taylor expansion yields r(r'+2)=r^2(q-S). For nonzero r, cancellation in R[x] gives r'+2=r(q-S); the ensuing degree comparison forces either r to be constant or r'=-2, producing exactly p(x)=x+c and p(x)=-x+c. The sufficiency checks provide valid polynomial choices of q in all cases. The proof is self-contained, contains no prohibited justification patterns, and uses no external or fact-graph references requiring validation.
